title: “IF YOU HAD BEEN HERE…”
paragraphs: “IF YOU HAD BEEN HERE…”
Four words.

Not a prayer.
Not a sermon.
A wound.

Martha didn’t whisper it politely.
She threw it into the air like broken glass.

“Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.”
— John 11:21
Feel the tension.

She believed in Jesus…
but she was also disappointed in Him.

Lazarus was sick.
Word had been sent.
Jesus knew.
And still… He waited.
Four days in the grave.
The smell of death already creeping through the tomb.
And Martha runs to meet Him — heart pounding, grief boiling over.
“IF YOU HAD BEEN HERE…”
You can almost hear what she didn’t say.

If You had cared.
If You had come sooner.
If You hadn’t delayed.
If You loved us like we thought.
Painful honesty.
Some of us have prayed the same sentence… just with different words.
“Lord, if You had been here… my marriage wouldn’t have collapsed.”
“Lord, if You had been here… my father wouldn’t have died.”
“Lord, if You had been here… my life wouldn’t look like this.”
Faith.
Mixed with accusation.
But watch Jesus.
He does not rebuke her.
He does not shame her grief.
He meets her right in the middle of it and says something that shakes the grave itself:

“I am the resurrection and the life.
Whoever believes in Me, though he die, yet shall he live.”
— John 11:25
Jesus didn’t just come to prevent a funeral.
He came to conquer death.
Martha thought the miracle was late.
But Jesus was preparing something bigger than healing.
Resurrection.
And before the stone rolled away…
Before Lazarus walked out…
Jesus asked her a question that still echoes today:
“Do you believe this?”

Not: Do you understand this?
Not: Are you emotionally ready for this?
Do you believe?
Friend, sometimes God feels late.
But the cross looked late too.
The disciples thought the story was over.
Yet three days later…
The stone moved.
The grave lost.
And death bowed to Jesus Christ.
So if your heart has ever whispered,
“Lord… if You had been here…”
Hear this truth:
He is here.

Even at the tomb.
Even in the delay.
Even in the grief.
And the One standing before the grave still says:
“I am the resurrection and the life.”
Believe Him.
Because Jesus doesn’t just arrive at broken stories.
He rewrites them.
